scenes.text: This lake killed seventeen hundred people. And it works exactly like a soda bottle.
Deep down, the water holds huge amounts of carbon dioxide, trapped by pressure.
Disturb it, and the gas rushes out all at once.
In 1986, Lake Nyos in Cameroon did exactly that. One night. One burst. Seventeen hundred dead.
Today, pipes let the gas out slowly, so the bottle never pops again. Full story on Oddly Logical Science. Subscribe for more true stories this strange.
